name: position
summary: Sets position and offsets in one call, using shorthand order.

arguments.name: $position
accepts: static, relative, absolute, fixed or sticky, in any case, or a vendor keyword such as -webkit-sticky
a quoted keyword is written without its quotes; any other word is refused, because the declaration would be dropped

arguments.name: $offsets
accepts: one to four lengths in shorthand order, or auto/inherit/initial/0
null in any position to leave that edge out

arguments.name: $logical
accepts: false, the default, for top, right, bottom and left
true for inset-block-start, inset-inline-end, inset-block-end and inset-inline-start, which follow the writing direction

caveats: `static` writes no offsets, because a static box ignores all four. Measured in Chrome 152, Firefox 156 and Safari 26.6.2, a static box carrying `top/right/bottom/left: 30px` sits exactly where a static box with none sits, while the same offsets move a `relative` box by 30px. Until 4.0.0 the default `0` meant every `position(static)` wrote four dead declarations. An offset that is not zero raises rather than being dropped quietly.

The mixin writes declarations, so it needs a rule to write them into. A call at the root failed with Sass's own "Declarations may only be used within style rules", which pointed at a line inside the library; it raises with the mixin's own message since 4.0.0.
